prize_parts.citation: for methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets and dynamic industries

statement.case_for: B047 has the clearest combination of a well-defined methodological discovery, a tight three-person credit core and thirty years of confirmation. The random-coefficients demand framework with endogenous prices (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995) and the dynamic-oligopoly estimation line (Pakes) turned empirical industrial organisation into a quantitative field. The tools are used routinely in merger review, antitrust, regulation, auctions, trade and health. The credit logic is also unusually clean for this list: the three names correspond to specific, identifiable papers and are not a bundle of separate strands. The field has had no recent recognition. I apply the same criteria I would apply to a candidate in my own field of political science, and merit here does not depend on that field.
statement.case_against: The credit boundary is not fully settled. A three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss, whose empirical entry and market-structure work is a distinct and earlier strand, and also Benkard and Levin on dynamic estimation. The results also depend on structural functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, and a committee could reasonably see the achievement as a method more than a substantive discovery. Finally, B047 has narrower opening support than B006 or B023, with six members ranking it. I treat that as information about how other members see it, not as evidence of merit, but it means my preference could be a minority view that the committee's discussion should test.

responses.point: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) are the clear originators of the collateral-based credit-cycle mechanism. Adding Gertler and Gilchrist would draw on the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator line, which overlaps with Bernanke's 2022 prize, so a two-person award is the cleanest attribution.
responses.response: I find this the most persuasive attribution argument on the table for B006. A two-name Kiyotaki-Moore award avoids the awkward question of crediting Gertler for work shared with an existing laureate, and the mechanism is foundational and has been tested since 2008. I did not rank B006 in my opening, and your argument is why I now list it as an alternative. I remain unsure that a two-person macro-finance award is more compelling than B047. The 2022 prize is adjacent, and the empirical identification of the collateral channel is, as you note, mixed. B047 has a more settled empirical record and has been used directly in policy practice, which is why I keep it first.

responses.point: BLP is a compact, clear core of three, and Pakes also made the foundational dynamic-industry contributions. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin made real but more distinct contributions, and the open question is whether the committee prefers to honour the empirical-IO tradition or the dynamic-games work alongside BLP.
responses.response: I agree with the three-name core and with your framing of the open question. My reading is that the demand-estimation breakthrough and Pakes's dynamic work are the best-defined achievement, and the Bresnahan-Reiss entry work is more naturally a separate and earlier tradition. Adding it would blur the citation. The cost is real, though. Leaving Bresnahan out of a prize on the broader structural-IO tradition would be a visible omission, and I cannot settle that from the shortlist alone. I would want the committee to confirm that the citation is for estimation methods and not for the whole field.

responses.point: B023 combines the task-based and skill-biased technology work with the China-shock evidence. It is conceptually clear, empirically credible and widely replicated, though the choice between Dorn and Katz within the three-person limit is a judgement call.
responses.response: I take the policy and empirical weight of B023 seriously, and I ranked it eighth only because of the attribution structure. The technology strand (Autor, Katz) and the trade-shock strand (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) are different discoveries with partly different people, and you share this concern in asking whether the committee sees them as one. I would resist treating the breadth of public influence as a substitute for a single sharp, attributable result. If the committee wants a labour award, I would favour a citation limited to the trade-shock strand, where credit is clearer, over a bundle that omits Dorn or Katz. I do not think that makes it stronger than B047 on attribution, but I accept it is stronger on policy reach.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat B047 as industrial organisation or as econometric methodology, and how it should be compared with other methods candidates.
Whether Bresnahan and Reiss should be credited alongside the BLP group, which a three-name cap forces me to exclude.
Whether Kiyotaki-Moore, with or without Gertler, is judged sufficiently distinct from the 2022 prize to outrank B047. I am not confident I weigh B006 correctly, and it was not in my opening ranking.
My assessments rely on general knowledge of the literatures and not on verified citation data or source checks.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to B047 is apparent from my profile. For the record, B021 (not my preferred choice) is a different case: my profile lists a corruption paper co-authored with Persson and Rothstein and long-standing work close to that literature, and I presented the 2024 prize on institutions. I disclose this and do not adjudicate it. Disclosing it is one reason I do not make B021 my preferred or alternative choice.
